rv.q: Cooke's production, ingeniously designed by Tom Pye, also offers a cornucopia of good performances.
It's vivacious and mischievous, yet often heavy-handed. And the screwy ending is completely misjudged.
Bruce Norris has the greater skill of skewering his targets with comic precision.

cn.t: Norris's ambitious three-hour satire on capitalism and free market economics impresses with its epic scale and picaresque style, though the execution doesn't quite match the grand vision.
